scope: arXiv:2310.09933v3, Eqs. (15)–(22), (23), (26a,b), Case Studies I–III and equilibrium checks in Appendix A. One converter and one infinite bus in the grid-synchronous frame, continuous averaged dynamics.

base.initialization: Lift the exact pre-dip equilibrium with zero resonant integrators for omega_delta=0. When multiple pre-dip equilibria exist, use the unique locally attracting branch for the selected order. Integrate the post-dip interval with switched forcing and prepend the constant pre-dip state.

angle.selection_evidence: Table III and Eq. (16) use r_g + j omega_g l_g, Table IV says match the impedance angle, and Fig. 7 states voltage bound 1.07 pu. The literal substitution of the printed l_g in s/rad is a separate sensitivity.

case_ii.certificate: Supremum of the sufficient Eq. (26a,b) bound as c_1 approaches the Eq. (23) margin from below and epsilon approaches 3 from above. An open upper bound. Paper does not state numerical c_1 or epsilon.
case_ii.additional_rg_020_angle: Retain case I phi as a diagnostic in addition to recalculating the matched phi for the changed r_g.

algebra_checks.classical_example: Appendix A Example 3, p_star=q_star=0, alpha=v_star=1, phi=pi/2, vg=0.1, rg=xg=0.4. Interpret 0.4 pu as reactance and use Eq. (40).
algebra_checks.triple_root_case: Construct a positive-grid example with alpha=v_star=vg=1, z=0.8+j0.6, matched rotation, rotated normalized setpoint 1.5+j sqrt(3)/2, and omega_delta=0, which gives (s-1)^3.

revision.reason: Initial run found three pre-dip equilibria in Case III with alpha=3. Fig. 7 starts on the only locally stable branch, near 0.595+j0.815 pu. The voltage dip itself, all parameter values and tolerances remain the same.

solver_refinement.reason: Initial BDF comparison missed the predeclared full-state tolerance only in the extended Case II 0.101 run. Targeted BDF refinement reduced the discrepancy, so the tighter reference tolerance is used across the final runs.
